reasons: The page is very large and handles many features in one function, which makes it hard to check by reading.
The state variable named window shadows the browser object.
No tests are visible for this file.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of the screen, such as a panel or button group.
Values the page remembers while it runs, such as the current filters or open signal.
A query reads saved data from the server; a mutation sends a change to it.
Asking the server for fresh data again at a set interval.
Rebuilding a component from scratch, which clears its state. Changing the key forces this.
A copy of server data kept in memory so the page does not need to fetch it again.
Linking signals to the project records in Yard.
A value in the web address, such as demo=1, that changes how a page opens.

sections.name: File setup, Stream, View, VIEWS
sections.title: Imports, view types and analysis tabs
sections.what: Brings in the React tools, the page's helper components and data functions, and the stylesheet. Defines the three signal streams (all, announcements, megaprojects), the ten analysis views, and the list of tabs with their display names.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the list of tabs in one place, so the tab bar and the views agree.
sections.watch_out: A view id must match the id used in other files, such as the hint code. A typo leaves a tab with no content.

sections.name: CUSTOMISE
sections.title: Which codebook sections each view can edit
sections.what: For each analysis view that has a Customise button, lists which codebook tabs it opens, such as solutions and triggers for the solution views, and signal types with the new-project test for the types view.
sections.why: Lets a visitor edit only the rules that define the view they are looking at.
sections.watch_out: The tab ids must match the tab ids in the codebook editor, or the button opens the wrong place.

sections.name: OpportunityMapPage
sections.title: Page entry point with demo switch
sections.what: Reads the demo flag from the web address and passes it to the workspace. The workspace is given a key that changes between demo and live, so switching rebuilds it from scratch.
sections.why: The file's comment says the key rebuild is how leaving the demo restores live state.
sections.watch_out: Because the key change rebuilds the workspace, any unsaved work on the page is lost when switching modes.

sections.name: Workspace, tool (part 1)
sections.title: Workspace setup, saved data and actions
sections.what: Creates the workspace: loads saved data (live or demo), polls for updates while background work runs, and sets up the starting filters, sort, view, page and popups. Defines the server actions for refresh, accounts, locations, settings, codebook save and reset, reclassification and Yard sync, and for demo mode, the messages that replace them.
sections.why: Likely reason: the workspace is where the page keeps all its shared state. The demo cache is kept separate so edits never reach live data.
sections.watch_out: The state named window shadows the browser's window object for the whole workspace function, so code here cannot use the real browser window.

sections.name: Workspace, tool (part 2)
sections.title: Preparing the signal list and AI search
sections.what: Applies the filters, sorts the signals by the chosen order, and builds the announcement, megaproject and company-mix lists. Runs the AI search and falls back to keyword matching when it is not set up. Also prepares the region counts, the opened signal and the auto-open for the demo.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list, counts and search results must all come from the same filtered set so they agree.
sections.watch_out: The AI search error is recognised by matching words such as 503 or not configured in the message, so changing the server's error wording would change which message the visitor sees.

sections.name: Workspace, tool (part 3)
sections.title: Search bar, citations and filter helpers
sections.what: Finishes matching signals to Yard projects and counts unmatched ones. Opens the citation drawer for a source, applies filter changes, lists the active filter chips with readable labels, and passes demo hints to the page. Starts the search form and filter controls that make up the page's top bar.
sections.why: Lets a visitor see exactly where each fact comes from and clear filters with one click.
sections.watch_out: Chip labels are looked up from the saved codebook, so a label that is missing from the codebook shows the raw id instead.

sections.name: Workspace, tool (part 4)
sections.title: Filter chips, panels, popups and footer
sections.what: Shows the filter chips that a user can remove, then the Signals panel and the Map and analysis panel. It also holds the popup windows for filters, research, the codebook and signal evidence, plus a footer with research queue counts and a Codebook button. A short status message and a citation popup sit at the end.
sections.why: Likely reason: the main screen is split into two panels, and the less-used tools open as popups so the main view stays uncluttered.
sections.watch_out: In demo mode, the research and codebook actions call helpers such as off and demoCodebook instead of changing real data, so test with demo mode off to see real behaviour.

sections.name: Workspace, tool (part 5)
sections.title: Tool registration record
sections.what: Describes this tool to the rest of the app: its short name, a one-line subtitle, the LIVE status label, its icon, its web address and the page component to show. Other parts of the app read this record to list the tool and open it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app finds its tools through a list of records like this one, so each tool declares itself here.
sections.watch_out: The slug and path must match the app's routing, which is not in this file, or the tool link will break.

summary: The main page of the Opportunity Map. It loads the saved signal data, applies filters, shows the signal list and analysis tabs, runs the AI search and Yard matching, and handles every action the owner takes, switching to a read-only demo mode when asked.
purpose: Gives the owner one screen to review sourced signals, manage the codebook and research, and open the advisor, news, profile and detail views.
why: Likely reason: the tool groups every Opportunity Map feature on one page, with a demo mode that reuses the same screen. The code does not state this.
how: 1. The page reads a demo flag from the web address and remounts the workspace when it changes. 2. The workspace loads saved data, polls while background work is running, and sets up filters, view and page. 3. Actions such as refresh, codebook save, status change and Yard sync are sent to the server, or blocked with a message in demo mode. 4. Filters produce the signal list, which is sorted, matched to Yard projects and shown alongside the analysis tabs. 5. Demo hints are added when in demo mode.
inputs: The page address (including demo and page parameters), the saved signal data from the server, the portfolio of Yard projects, the user's filters, weights, sort order and typed questions.
outputs: The rendered Opportunity Map page, with signal lists, analysis views, popups, citations and status messages, plus server requests for changes made in the live workspace.
risks: Inside the workspace function, the state named window hides the browser's own window object, so code there cannot reach the real browser window. Live polling settings that misread the queue fields could cause constant refreshing or no refreshing at all. Demo mode blocks most writes but relies on its own messages to explain this.
debug: If the page does not load, check the saved-data request and the error message shown. If the list is empty, check the status and industry filters. If the page refreshes too often, check the polling condition in the state query. If a demo action does nothing, check the off or demo branch for that action.
